events.title: Columbus lands on Puerto Rico
events.description: On his second voyage, Christopher Columbus landed on the island the Taíno called Borikén and named it San Juan Bautista. The name of its port, Puerto Rico, later passed to the whole island.

events.title: The Jay Treaty is signed in London
events.description: John Jay and Lord Grenville signed a treaty settling disputes left over from the Revolutionary War, including British forts in the north-west. Unpopular in America, it nonetheless averted war with Britain.

events.title: Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address
events.description: At the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery, Abraham Lincoln spoke for about two minutes. His short address recast the Civil War as a struggle for 'a new birth of freedom' and government 'of the people'.
events.html: At the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery, Abraham Lincoln spoke for about two minutes. His short address recast the Civil War as a struggle for 'a new birth of freedom' and government 'of the people'.

events.title: The Red Army launches Operation Uranus at Stalingrad
events.description: Soviet forces attacked the weak Romanian-held flanks north and south of Stalingrad. Within four days they encircled the German Sixth Army, which surrendered in February 1943.
events.html: Soviet forces attacked the weak Romanian-held flanks north and south of Stalingrad. Within four days they encircled the German Sixth Army, which surrendered in February 1943.

events.title: Anwar Sadat becomes the first Arab leader to visit Israel
events.description: Egypt's president Anwar Sadat flew to Israel and the next day addressed the Knesset in Jerusalem. His visit led to the Camp David Accords and the 1979 Egyptian-Israeli peace treaty.
